newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriot pilgrimage goes ahead despite ban.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriot pilgrimage goes ahead despite ban.

text.p: An Easter pilgrimage by Greek Cypriots in Turkish-held northern Cyprus went ahead on Sunday despite a dispute which had threatened to doom the rare cross-border visit, Turkish Cypriot officials said.
The officials said 118 pilgrims were attending ceremonies at the monastery of Apostolos Andreas, 120 km (75 miles) from Nicosia on the island's northeastern tip, to celebrate Greek Orthodox Easter.

An estimated 600 people were scheduled to take part in the visit when it was cancelled on Friday after Turkish Cypriot authorities refused to allow three of the proposed visitors to cross into the Turkish-held northern part of the island.

"It is pleasing that the visit is taking place. I wish all of them could come, but they are banned by the Greek Cypriot authorities," said Taner Etkin, foreign minister in the self-styled Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus which is recognised only by Turkey.

Greek Cypriot authorities objected to the restrictions on the proposed visitors and said they had cancelled the trip. Efforts through the United Nations to get the Turkish Cypriots to lift the ban failed.

Etkin said 49 pilgrims crossed into the northern part of the island on Saturday and 69 on Sunday. A further 80 Greek Cypriots had applied to cross into northern Cyprus on Monday to visit relatives there, he said.

It was the first such visit since the island's division in 1974 after a Turkish invasion sparked by a brief coup by the military then ruling in Greece. More than 2,000 people had initially applied to go.
The pilgrimage was in response to a visit by 435 Turkish Cypriot pilgrims to a mosque in the Greek Cypriot south last week to celebrate the Moslem Eid al-Adha feast.
Such visits are part of several planned events over the next few months aimed at promoting goodwill between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities.
